long_biography.plain_text:
Frederiksen began as a trainee at Matas and became an independent retailer at 27. He expanded one health-and-beauty shop into a group of stores, accumulating a substantial holding in the nationwide chain. The 2007 sale of a majority stake to CVC Capital Partners converted that long operating career into capital for a second phase as an investor.

Hospitality and historic-property projects became Frederiksen's main outlet for reinvestment. He acquired and restored Molskroen, its Strandhotel, Hotel Bretagne and Havreholm Castle. He paired these ventures with a celebrated collection of rare pre-war automobiles assembled with his wife, Vivi. After her death, he dispersed the collection and gradually divested much of the hotel portfolio, closing a career defined by retail building, reinvestment and preservation.

uncertainties.detail: Henrik Frederiksen is a common Danish name, but the resolved person is supported by an unusually specific bridge. Northern Grace's own history names Vivi Henriksen's new husband Henrik as buyer; ship chronology places him in Ebeltoft after her death; corporate filings pair Vivi Henriksen Frederiksen and Henrik at Mercandia Invest and Molskroen; the family notice calls him Matas Materialist; and auction material identifies the collection he assembled with Vivi. Other Henrik Frederiksen directors, athletes and professionals lack this spouse, vessel, Matas, Ebeltoft and collection combination and are excluded.

The immutable input records a current Northern Grace relationship beginning in April 2015. Public vessel sources identify the same ship under its former name Zar, place Frederiksen's ownership around Vivi's death and report transfer to an association by June 2021, followed by Northern Survey. These sources make the identity bridge exceptionally strong but indicate the upstream current flag may be stale. No shared input or live vessel relationship is changed.

The source display name embeds Mr even though the Title field already stores Mr separately. All reviewed public sources use Henrik Frederiksen without an embedded honorific. The owner object preserves the immutable source display, while a reviewable correction to Henrik Frederiksen is proposed to prevent title duplication.

Independent reporting confirms his death at 81 through partner Susanne Risom. Mortality and the complete birth date are proposed at 100 confidence; the death date and age are retained as a sequenced review candidate until mortality is corrected and the fields become applicable. No place of birth or death is inferred.

The biographies therefore say a group of stores and avoid an exact count. The Matas transaction is company-level evidence and no reported consideration is converted into personal proceeds.

His later career covered hotel ownership, restoration, property, holdings and automotive interests, and he sold Molskroen in 2025 while other assets were being divested. Diversified is used for Primary Industry because no single operating sector is evidenced as dominant at his February 2026 death.
